question: What the parcel hub's engineer needs is the total energy in kilojoules for 10 identical sorting lines, each running 9 identical carts. Each cart has a mass of 12 kg and is 1 m long. It moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the number of ways of choosing 2 items from a set of 9. Find the kinetic energy of one cart in joules, multiply by 9 for the carts on one line, and convert to kilojoules. Multiply by 10 for all the lines. What is the total in kJ?

The number the fleet engineer ultimately wants is the total on-board energy in kilojoules for 6 identical depots, each with 8 identical test vehicles. Each vehicle has a mass of 54000 g and moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the rate of change of the curve 3x^3 + 5x^2 with respect to x at x = 1. Find the vehicle's kinetic energy in joules and convert it to kilojoules. Add 26 kJ for the charge in the vehicle's battery, multiply by 8 for the vehicles at one depot, and then by 6 for all the depots. What is the total in kJ?

A 47000 g test sled on a track 90 m long moves at a speed in metres per second found by taking the sum of the first 8 odd numbers, adding 8, and subtracting 7. Find the sled's kinetic energy in joules and convert it to kilojoules. The track's monitor subtracts 15 kJ for the energy absorbed by the arresting gear. What is the resulting figure in kJ?

A 28000 g test cart on a track 12 m long moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the second derivative of 2x^3 - 6x^2 with respect to x evaluated at x = 2. Find the cart's kinetic energy in joules. The rig runs 8 identical carts, so multiply by 8. The energy log subtracts 5 J for the energy lost in the couplings and adds 27 J for the energy stored in the end buffers. What is the final energy figure in J?

A warehouse tug pulls a 72 kg trolley along an aisle 40 m long with an acceleration in metres per second squared equal to the area under the curve 1x^2 + 4x between x = 3 and x = 4. Find the force in newtons needed for that acceleration and subtract 30 N for the assistance of the aisle's slight downhill slope. The tug pulls 2 such trolleys, so multiply by 2, and convert the total to kilonewtons. The warehouse runs 11 identical tugs, so multiply by 11. What is the total force in kN?

A quarry's haul truck tows a 197000 g test trailer across a yard 200 m wide. The trailer accelerates at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the greatest common divisor of 165 and 317. Find the force in newtons needed for one trailer. The truck tows 7 such trailers, so multiply by 7, and convert the total to kilonewtons. The quarry runs 7 identical trucks, so multiply by 7. Then add 13 kN for the drag of the yard's gravel surface. What is the total force in kN?

The number the bench technician wants is the total energy in kilojoules for 10 identical test runs, each corrected for two losses. In each run a 3 kg slider, which is 15 cm long, moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0. Find the slider's kinetic energy in joules, subtract 7 J for the energy lost to rail friction, and subtract 27 J for the energy absorbed by the end stop. Convert the corrected figure to kilojoules, and multiply by 10 for all the runs. What is the total in kJ?

A 21 kg test carriage on a wind-tunnel rail moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the area under the curve 4x^2 + 6x between x = 2 and x = 3. Find the carriage's kinetic energy in joules at that speed. The tunnel runs 5 identical carriages in a batch, so multiply by 5, and convert the total to kilojoules. The facility runs 6 identical batches, so multiply by 6. What is the total in kJ?

A shipyard's slipway winch pulls a 120 kg test cradle up a ramp 30 m long. The cradle accelerates at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the rate of change of the curve 5x^3 + 1x^2 with respect to x at x = 2. Find the force in newtons needed for that acceleration and convert it to kilonewtons. A 17 kN buoyancy assist is subtracted to give one winch's net demand. The yard has 11 identical winches, and it runs 2 identical shifts; multiply by 11 and then by 2. What is the total net demand in kN (negative if the buoyancy assist dominates)?

The figure the rigging inspector wants is the total load in kilonewtons for a set of 7 identical hoists after a 27 kN allowance for the headframe is added. Each hoist raises a 23000 g platform with an acceleration in metres per second squared equal to the number of ways of choosing 4 items from a set of 8. Find the force in newtons needed for one platform, add 27 N for the drag of its guide, and convert the result to kilonewtons. Multiply by 7 for all the hoists, and add the 27 kN headframe allowance. What is the total load in kN?

A 47000 g sled on a track 55 m long moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the rate of change of the curve 3x^3 + 6x^2 with respect to x at x = 2. Find the sled's kinetic energy in joules and subtract 18 J for the energy lost in the starting gate. The rig runs 12 identical sleds, so multiply by 12, and convert the total to kilojoules. Then subtract 17 kJ for the energy absorbed by the shared arresting gear. What is the resulting total in kJ?

The value the foundry manager wants is the total force in newtons for a line of 12 identical pushers, after allowances of 21 N and 17 N for the line's guards are added. Each pusher moves a 165 kg mould, which is 80 cm wide, with an acceleration in metres per second squared equal to the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0. Find the force in newtons needed for one mould and multiply by 12 for all the pushers. Then add 21 N for the entry guard and 17 N for the exit guard. What is the total in N?

A 37000 g test cart moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the greatest common divisor of 279 and 276. Find the cart's kinetic energy in joules. The rig runs 8 identical carts, so multiply by 8, and subtract 22 J for the energy absorbed by the shared end buffer. The lab performs 8 identical runs, so multiply by 8. What is the total energy in J?

A 25 kg tool carriage on a workshop rail 6 m long moves at a speed in metres per second equal to 4 less than the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0. Find the carriage's kinetic energy in joules. The workshop runs 4 identical carriages, so multiply by 4, and subtract 11 J for the energy absorbed by the rail's end stops. Convert the result to kilojoules. What is the total in kJ?

The figure the crane supervisor ultimately needs is the total force in kilonewtons for 4 identical cranes, each corrected for sling friction and a counter-jib assist. Each crane raises a 112000 g test block with an upward acceleration in metres per second squared equal to the sum of the first 5 odd numbers. Find the force in newtons needed for one block, subtract 22 N for the assistance of the crane's counter-jib, and add 28 N for the sling friction. Convert the corrected figure to kilonewtons, and multiply by 4 for all the cranes. What is the total in kN?

The number the rig engineer needs is the force in kilonewtons required to drive a test sled. The sled has a mass of 105000 g and a length of 3 m. Its acceleration in metres per second squared is found by taking the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 24 = 0, multiplying it by 9, and adding 8. Find the force in newtons needed for that acceleration, and convert it to kilonewtons. What is the required force in kN?

The figure the technician wants is the net energy change in kilojoules of a rig's battery after three transactions. The rig's cart has a mass of 9 kg and moves at a speed in metres per second equal to 5 times the sum of 2 and 1. Find the cart's kinetic energy in joules, which the brake recovers into the battery, and convert it to kilojoules. The battery then supplies 7 kJ to the heater, receives 29 kJ from the charger, and supplies 26 kJ to the motor. What is the net change in kJ (negative if a loss)?

A 33000 g test sled on a track 70 m long moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the area under the curve 5x^2 + 6x between x = 0 and x = 2. Find the sled's kinetic energy in joules. The rig runs 3 identical sleds, so multiply by 3, and add 29 J for the energy stored in the shared launch spring. The lab performs 9 identical runs, so multiply by 9. What is the total energy in J?

The number the warehouse supervisor wants is the total force in newtons for 9 identical conveyor lines, each with 4 identical pushers and a 7 N allowance for its end guard. Each pusher moves a 72 kg crate with an acceleration in metres per second squared equal to the greatest common divisor of 312 and 158. Find the force in newtons needed for one crate, multiply by 4 for the pushers on one line, and add the 7 N allowance. Multiply by 9 for all the lines. What is the total in N?

A school rocketry club fires a 4 kg model rocket from a launch rail that is 2 m tall. The rocket's mass includes its recovery parachute. Its speed at the top of the rail, in metres per second, is set by the club's controller as follows: take the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 7x + 6 = 0, multiply it by 7, subtract 8, add 23, and then add 8. Using the rocket's mass and that speed, find its kinetic energy as it leaves the rail. What is the rocket's kinetic energy in J?

A dockside crane raises a 120 kg test block, which is 1 m across, with an upward acceleration in metres per second squared equal to 24 more than the number of ways of choosing 4 items from a set of 6. Find the force in newtons needed for one block. The crane lifts 8 such blocks on one spreader, so multiply by 8, and convert the total to kilonewtons. The spreader's own hardware adds 29 kN, so add 29 kN. What is the total hook load in kN?

A lab's linear actuator pushes a 15 kg carriage along a rail 5 m long with an acceleration in metres per second squared equal to the area under the curve 3x^2 + 1x between x = 0 and x = 4. Find the force in newtons needed for that acceleration. A return spring assists with 17 N, so subtract 17 N, and the rail's friction adds 27 N, so add 27 N. Convert the result to kilonewtons. The lab has 8 identical actuators, so multiply by 8. What is the total force in kN?

On a laboratory test track, a sled with a mass of 39000 g is held at rest until t = 1 s and then released, and from t = 1 s to t = 2 s its acceleration in m/s² follows 3t² + 8t, with t in seconds. The sled itself is 1.2 m long. At the instant t = 2 s a booster fires and multiplies the sled's speed by exactly 2. The engineer wants the energy the sled carries purely because of its motion right after the booster, but reduced by the 29 J that the rails have already turned into heat. What is that remaining energy, in kJ?

A shipyard engineer needs the total force, in N, that 3 identical winch assemblies must supply together, where each winch drives 9 identical cables and each cable hauls 10 identical crates. Work back from the single crate: every crate has a mass of 148 kg, and the system must give each crate an acceleration, in m/s², equal to the largest whole number that divides both 170 and 229 with no remainder. The force on one crate is whatever is needed to produce that acceleration. A cable's pull is the combined force on its 10 crates, a winch's output is the combined pull of its 9 cables, and the 3 winches together give the figure required. What is that total force, in N?

The number a drone team must report is a total energy budget in kJ, built as follows: the energy of motion of 8 identical drones, plus 22 kJ held in a spare battery pack, plus a further 26 kJ stored in the ground station's capacitor bank. Each drone has a mass of 14000 g and cruises at a speed, in m/s, equal to the number of different ways of choosing 2 waypoints out of 7. The hangar is kept at 18 °C throughout the test. Work out one drone's energy of motion and convert it to kJ before combining the 8 drones and then adding the two reserves in turn. What is the total budget, in kJ?
